CausalChain: AHNAK2 upregulation -> Direct interaction with geranylgeranyltransferase enzymes (+ integration with NAA40, NEK2, circRNA-AHNAK pathways) -> Altered protein geranylgeranylation of Rho/Ras GTPases -> Disrupted membrane localization and signal transduction -> Cooperative modulation of vesicular trafficking via RAB proteins -> Increased cell motility, angiogenesis, and metastasis -> Adverse liver neoplasm prognosis
Hypothesis: We hypothesize that in liver neoplasms, overexpression of AHNAK2 acts synergistically with established oncogenic signals to modulate protein geranylgeranylation. Specifically, AHNAK2 is proposed to interact directly with geranylgeranyltransferase enzymes, leading to selective changes in the lipid modification of key signaling proteins such as Rho and Ras GTPases. This alteration disrupts their membrane localization and downstream signaling and, through cooperative interactions with RAB family proteins, enhances vesicular trafficking. Moreover, by contextualizing AHNAK2 within a network of complementary oncogenic mechanisms (including those mediated by NAA40, NEK2, and circRNA-driven AHNAK regulation), we propose that these combined molecular events culminate in increased cellular motility, angiogenesis, and metastasis, thereby contributing to an aggressive liver cancer phenotype. Systematic evaluation of this hypothesis will be performed using state-of-the-art CRISPR/Cas9 screening, proximity-labeling mass spectrometry, live-cell imaging, and integrated proteogenomic profiling.
Abstract: In liver neoplasms, aggressive tumor behavior appears to be driven by interconnected mechanisms. We propose that overexpression of AHNAK2 not only directly modulates protein geranylgeranylation but also integrates with other oncogenic drivers – such as NAA40-mediated epigenetic changes, NEK2-driven signaling, and circRNA-regulated AHNAK axes – to amplify malignant progression. Specifically, AHNAK2 is hypothesized to physically interact with geranylgeranyltransferase enzymes, thereby selectively altering the lipid modification of critical signaling proteins like Rho and Ras GTPases. This modified post-translational process disrupts normal membrane localization, perturbs signal transduction, and, in cooperation with specific RAB family proteins, enhances vesicular trafficking. Leveraging contemporary techniques including CRISPR/Cas9 knockout screens, proximity-labeling mass spectrometry (e.g., BioID), live-cell imaging, and integrated proteogenomic analyses, this study aims to decouple the multifaceted contributions of AHNAK2 from parallel oncogenic pathways, thereby uncovering novel therapeutic targets and biomarkers in liver cancer.
Orignal_vs_New: The original hypothesis linked AHNAK2 overexpression solely to altered geranylgeranylation and subsequent impacts on Rho/Ras GTPases and vesicular trafficking. In our revised hypothesis, we explicitly integrate additional, well-supported oncogenic mechanisms (such as NAA40-mediated epigenetic dysregulation, NEK2-driven signaling, and circRNA-regulated AHNAK expression) to create a multifactorial model. This unified framework preserves the original causal chain—AHNAK2 upregulation leading to altered geranylgeranylation, disrupted signaling, and aggressive tumor behavior—while broadening the mechanistic context and employing contemporary technological approaches to enhance practical implementability and reflect the complexity observed in liver neoplasms.
